payload.summary: Amendment fr-2 identifies a genuine test correctness issue: the test helper uses hardcoded approximate constants (2.497, 4.118) while the implementation derives more precise values from molar masses (2.49730..., 4.11796...), producing a ~3.27e-4 discrepancy that far exceeds the 1e-9 tolerance. This is a real defect that should be fixed — either by updating the test constants to match the implementation's molar-mass-derived values, or by relaxing the tolerance. The molar-mass-based implementation is chemically more accurate, so updating the test is the right path.

votes.rationale: The amendment correctly identifies a real test defect. The test's expected_gh_d helper uses rounded constants (2.497, 4.118) that don't match the implementation's molar-mass-derived constants (100.0869/40.078 ≈ 2.49730, 100.0869/24.305 ≈ 4.11796), causing a ~3.27e-4 discrepancy against a 1e-9 tolerance. This is not a flaky or edge-case issue — the test will deterministically fail. The fix should update the test helper to use the same molar-mass-based constants as the implementation (which is chemically more precise), not loosen the tolerance to paper over the mismatch. Even though this is pre-existing and unrelated to the CO2 changes, it is a real broken test on the branch that warrants fixing.
